thinking_and_logic: Your solution keeps a hash map from value to its index for values encountered so far. For each number n at index i, it computes complement = target - n and checks whether that complement was seen earlier; if so, it immediately returns the pair of indices. Checking before inserting ensures you never pair an element with itself, aligning with the problem’s constraints and the answer key’s known pitfalls.
code_assessment: The final code is essentially identical to the canonical optimal solution in the answer key (single-pass hash map, complement check before insert), achieving O(n) time and O(n) space and preserving original indices (unlike sort-based approaches). It also avoids the 'same element twice' mistake by only matching against previously seen indices. The only minor concern is the fallback return [] which is fine under the given guarantee but would need a clearer contract (exception/None) for generalized versions.
